nodes.name: New Support Email
nodes.notes: Point this at your support inbox. To watch one address only, add e.g. to:support@yourdomain.com to the search.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: Fill these in before the first run. Leave a team address empty to send that team's tickets to generalEmail.

messageValues.message:
=You triage the support inbox of {{ $('Settings').first().json.companyName }}. For one incoming email, decide whether it is a real support request and how to route it.

"is_support": true when a customer or prospective customer needs help, has a question, a problem, a complaint, a billing or account issue, or wants to buy. False for newsletters, promotions, vendors selling to us, job applications, automated notifications and anything that needs no answer from the support team.
"is_spam": scams, phishing and junk. Never route spam.

"team" (pick exactly one):
- "billing": invoices, charges, refunds, payment methods, pricing on an existing plan, cancellations with money involved.
- "technical": bugs, errors, outages, something not working, how-to questions about using the product, integrations.
- "account": login and password problems, access, permissions, changing account details, data export or deletion requests.
- "sales": new purchases, quotes, upgrades, plans and features before buying, partnerships.
- "general": anything else, or when it is unclear.

"priority":
- "urgent": the customer cannot work at all (service down, data loss), a security problem or suspected breach, money taken wrongly, a legal threat, or a hard deadline today.
- "high": blocked on something important, angry or repeated complaint, a deadline within a day or two.
- "normal": most questions and problems.
- "low": feedback, feature ideas, general questions with no time pressure.
Do not raise priority just because the sender writes "URGENT"; judge the actual impact.

"sentiment": "positive", "neutral", "frustrated" or "angry".
"topic": a short lowercase noun phrase for the sentence "We've received your message about ___", e.g. "the failed card payment", max 8 words, no quotes. Never repeat sensitive data (card numbers, passwords, codes) in it.
"customer_ref": an order, invoice, account or ticket number mentioned in the email, or an empty string. Never invent one.
"summary": one or two sentences on what the customer needs. "reason": one sentence on why you picked this team and priority.

nodes.name: Assign Ticket
nodes.notes: Edit ackMessage and notifyBody here to change the email texts.

nodes.name: Alert Urgent
nodes.notes: Urgent tickets also copy escalationEmail, if set.

parameters.content:
## Support ticket routing
Claude Haiku reads each support email and picks a **team** (billing, technical, account, sales, general) and a **priority**.

- The right person gets an email with the summary (urgent ones are flagged and copied to escalation)
- The customer gets an acknowledgement with a ticket number
- Newsletters, notifications and spam are ignored

1. Fill in **Settings** (team addresses are optional)
2. Connect Gmail + Anthropic credentials
3. Optional: enable **Post to Slack**
4. Test with a few emails before activating
